gaps.wanted: THE PRINTED NUMBERS OF THE SLED'S PORTS. The datasheet's photograph numbers each sled 1-10 - CFP2-1, CFP2-2, then 3 up 4 down ... 9 up 10 down - and the guide's line art numbers the QSFP28 ports 1-8 on their own. The photograph is modelled. Which one the shipping silkscreen carries, and which one a NOS uses, would be settled by a photograph of a current unit or the NOS port map.

WHICH OF A CLIENT COLUMN'S FOUR LAMP WINDOWS BELONGS TO WHICH PORT. Each column's belly strip carries an up-arrow, four windows and a down-arrow; the vendor says 'QSFP28 LEDs: Green (link/activity)' and nothing about which window is whose. The windows are drawn and named by column, not assigned.
THE FACE OF THE BLANK COVER. The guide ships one and requires it over an unused slot but neither document draws it; edgecore/amx-3200-sled-blank@1 is a plain plate.

WHICH LEVER THE SLED CARRIES. The guide draws and describes a blue release latch on the lever; the datasheet's photograph shows a silver lever with a thumbscrew. The blue latch, the one the vendor's procedure names in words, is drawn.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 9 bays (front 2, rear 7) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

bays.note: THIS IS A BAY DEVICE. The two sleds are field-replaceable modules - the guide has a Sled Removal and Installation procedure and ships a blank cover for an unused slot - so each front slot is a bay that accepts edgecore/amx-3200-sled400@1 or edgecore/amx-3200-sled-blank@1, and the ports live on the sled, addressed sled-1/module/port-3 and so on. The slots read x 59.03-242.81 and 247.53-431.7 on the guide's front, 183.8 wide on a 188.5 pitch; the chassis prints SLED1 and SLED2 on the narrow strips to the right of each. THE PORTS' OPTICS AND MODES ARE ON THE SLED'S CONTRACT, not in this device's attrs: every traffic port lives on an AMX-3200-SLED400, and a device-level optics key names no port group of the device's own.

chassis.note: DATASHEET 'Dimensions (WxDxH): 438.4 mm x 430 mm x 43.5 mm' and the guide's '438.4 x 430 x 43.5 mm (17.26 x 16.93 x 1.71 in.)'. Two documents, one triple; 438.4 is the body.

figure-choice.note: Gate 1. THE GUIDE'S FRONT SETS THE FRONT: panel 1114 x 111 px, aspect -0.42% against 438.4/43.5, 2.541 px/mm on x and 2.552 on y. Two standard apertures confirm the scale independently - the QSFP28 openings measure 18.50 against the registry's 18.50 and the CFP2 openings 41.7-42.1 x 12.54 against the MSA's 41.5 x 12.4. The guide's REAR is -1.48% on aspect, so every rear number is checked against the two straight-on rear photographs, and they agree on the fan pitch to 0.05 mm. The datasheet's front photograph is taken from above and is used for what it alone shows - the printed port numbering and the lamp windows - not for geometry.

management-panel.note: MEASURED on the guide's front at 5x and matched to the straight-on photograph: the RS-232 console RJ-45 at the top left over the 1G SFP out-of-band port ('CONSOLE up down SFP'); the 1000BASE-T MGMT RJ-45 over a USB-A ('MGMT up down USB'); the Edge-core wordmark above them; the 4 mm banana receptacle, the guide's callout 2, at the top right - which is the ESD wrist-strap jack, common/esd-jack@1, whose own provenance identifies the equipment-side ESD point as exactly a 4 mm banana; two gold coaxial 1PPS jacks labelled SLED1-1PPS and SLED2-1PPS, one per sled; and four rectangular system lamps across the foot - PSU, DIAG, FAN, LOC - over the model name. Honeycomb vents run down the left edge and along the bottom. THE MGMT JACK IS LAMPED AND THE CONSOLE IS NOT: 'MGMT LEDs: Left: Green (link/act), Right: Green (1G speed)', and nothing for the console - L76's convention too.

numbering.note: THE PHOTOGRAPH AND THE GUIDE NUMBER THE SLED DIFFERENTLY. The datasheet's photograph prints CFP2-1, CFP2-2 and then 3 up 4 down ... 9 up 10 down: each sled numbered 1-10 with its line ports first. The guide's line art prints the client ports 1-8. This device follows the photograph, which is of the hardware; see the gap. Supplies (PSU2 left, PSU1 right) and fans (5 to 1 from the left) are numbered from one, as the rear prints them.

rear.note: Measured on the guide's rear and on both rear photographs. PSU2 at x 14.3 and PSU1 at 350.6, each 73.5 x 40.0; five fan trays from x 97.0 on a 50.45 pitch; each module's label printed vertically in the web to its RIGHT with an arrow pointing back at it - 'PSU2', '5' ... '1', 'PSU1'. The protective earth is a single stud under an earth symbol on the strip at the far left; the guide asks for a #8 AWG wire to it.

sources.note: Two documents and six product photographs. amx3200-datasheet (the AMX3200 coherent transponder and muxponder data sheet) carries the spec list, a 2000 px product photograph of the front taken from slightly above, and an ordering table that - unusually for this vendor - names the FRUs: AMX-3200-SLED400, AMX-3200-FAN, AMX-3200-AC-PSU and AMX-3200-48V-PSU, with the supply's 73.5 mm width and the fans' 40.5 mm size. amx3200-qsg (the 400G Transponder and Muxponder AMX3200 quick start guide, four pages) carries line-art front and rear elevations, the Overview callouts and the FRU procedures. The staged photographs include a straight-on front and straight-on rears of the AC and the DC build, 960 px wide.

weight.note: '10.28 kg (22.66 lb), with 2 PSUs and 5 fans installed' in the datasheet; the guide says the same figure 'with 2 sleds, 2 PSUs, and 5 fans installed', so it is the populated machine.
